provenance.instrument: City of Warren Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 470 Zoning, Ord. No. 1978 of 5-20-2024), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WA2487, City of Warren (Warren County named in 470-90 'Board' and 'Lot of record'). The district use table (470-16) and area regulations (470-15) are text. The only attachment is the table of zoning map amendments. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 260. Chapter page shows New Laws (0)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 chapter page, Version Information: 'Includes legislation through 08-17-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: 'Accessory dwelling unit' is a permitted (P) accessory use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU in the 470-16 use table. The chapter does not define it and gives it no standards: no size cap, no owner or family rule and no count per lot

A unit inside or attached to the house may instead be read as turning it into a multifamily dwelling ('a building having two or more dwelling units'), which R-1 does not permit (470-90, 470-16). Multifamily dwellings are permitted by right in R-2, R-3 and MU, so there that reading changes nothing. Ask the zoning officer which reading applies in R-1

The 470-34 multifamily standards (one acre, 12 units an acre, 50 ft from a lot line next to a single-family house) apply only where multifamily is a special exception or conditional use: 'The following regulations apply when the use is allowed by special exception or conditional use' (470-23.1). That is C-1 and Pres, not R-2, R-3 or MU
Only one principal structure is allowed on a lot, except in planned residential developments and for multifamily dwellings (470-20A). A unit in a separate building is an accessory structure

Residential districts: new lots 5,000 sq ft and 40 ft wide. Existing lots of 4,000 sq ft may be used. Front yard is the average of the block. Side and rear yards at least 5 ft. No building less than 10 ft from an adjoining building. Building cover 50%, 45% or 35% by lot size (470-15A). Exactly 10,000 sq ft falls in no tier. On a corner lot the front yard is the addressed side, and structures, fences included, may be built up to 50% of the side yard

On a lot less than 60 ft wide an accessory building needs 3 ft side and rear yards and may be one story, up to 20 ft (470-15A). No accessory height is given for wider lots, and no principal building height was found in 470-15

Minimum dwelling size: 500 sq ft for a single-family dwelling and 400 sq ft for a one-bedroom apartment in 470-15A, but 800 sq ft per single-family unit and 550 sq ft per multifamily unit in the 470-90 'Floor area' definition. Which minimum reaches the accessory unit itself is not settled

Parking: one space for each dwelling unit (470-69A(1)). No parking in the front yard in residential districts except on lots with two frontages or narrow side and rear yards (470-70A(2)). A residential parking area may be at most 440 sq ft, may not cover more than half the front of the house, and a driveway may be at most 18 ft wide, 30 ft combined (470-70A(4)). When an existing property is converted to more residential units and the lot lacks room, half of the on-site parking is waived (470-71). Spaces within 500 ft off the lot may count (470-72)
A family is related persons or up to four unrelated persons living as one housekeeping unit (470-90)

Nonconforming lot of record in separate ownership: a single-family house and customary accessory buildings may be built if the yards are met (470-77A). Contiguous lots in the same ownership merge (470-77B). Enlarging a nonconforming structure in a way that adds to the nonconformity needs a variance (470-76A)

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board under MPC 910.2 (470-83C(4)). No bar on a use variance. Uses called 'customary' or 'similar' are decided by the Zoning Officer (470-18A). A special exception lapses if no permit is taken out within 6 months (470-87A)

Floodplain rules are in Chapter 260 (260-21). Manufactured homes are barred in the floodway and within 50 ft of the top of bank in the floodplain (260-30). In Pres, the Planning Commission reviews any development (470-15D)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: City of Warren Department of Codes and Planning. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: the chapter page and its Version Information, Article IV (470-14 to 470-17, the use table by screen view), Article V, Article VI (470-23.1, 470-34, 470-36, 470-50, 470-54), Article VIII, Article IX, Article XI, Article XIII, Chapter 260 sections 21 and 30 and code searches. The code has no historic preservation chapter. 'Historic District' appears only in 470-90, 470-57 and 470-60 and in 310-2. Not read: Articles I to III, Article VII, Article X, Article XII and the rest of Chapter 260.

term.note: Listed in the 470-16 use table under 'Accessory'. Not defined in 470-90

status.note: 'P is permitted by right' (470-16A). P in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU

status_outside.note: C-1, C-2, I-1 and Pres do not list it. I-1 is meant 'to prohibit residential development' (470-14G)

path.note: A zoning permit from the Zoning Officer

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, under MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Multifamily dwelling (two or more units)
value.conditions: A building with two or more dwelling units (470-90). Permitted by right in R-2, R-3 and MU on the district lot: 5,000 sq ft for a new lot, an existing lot of 4,000 sq ft, 5 ft side and rear yards, building cover by lot size (470-15A). It is one of the cases where more than one principal structure may stand on a lot (470-20A). The one acre and 12 units an acre of 470-34 apply only where multifamily is a special exception, in C-1 and Pres (470-23.1)
value.note: A house turned into two units is this use if the unit is not read as an accessory dwelling unit. Not permitted in R-1

value.name: Apartment, second story and above
value.conditions: A dwelling above a nonresidential use in a mixed building (470-90). Also permitted in C-1 and C-2
value.note: Only above a nonresidential use, not over a house

historic_bypass.note: The code has no historic preservation chapter and no historic path. 'Historic District' is defined in 470-90 and used only in the sign and wireless rules (470-60, 470-57)

value.condition: A unit inside or attached to the house may make it 'a building having two or more dwelling units', a multifamily dwelling, which R-1 does not permit. A single-family detached dwelling contains one dwelling unit.

disputed_by.note: The use table lists 'Accessory dwelling unit' as a permitted accessory use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU, so a unit inside or attached to the house may be read as that accessory use and not as a multifamily dwelling.

value.condition: A unit in a separate building must be an accessory structure. 'Only one principal structure may be permitted on a lot, except in planned residential developments and for multifamily dwellings.'

In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction without a City or DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway, no more than one foot of rise, and no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a permit.

types_allowed.note: The unit is not defined, so no form is named or barred. An accessory structure may be 'attached, semidetached or detached'

setback_side_ft.note: 'Side and rear yard: Minimum of 5 feet'. On a lot less than 60 ft wide an accessory building may be 3 ft from the line

setback_rear_ft.note: On a lot less than 60 ft wide an accessory building may be 3 ft from the line

value.where: An accessory building on a lot less than 60 ft wide may be 3 ft from the side and rear lines and may be one story, up to 20 ft. This does not apply on a lot 60 ft wide or more, where the 5 ft yards hold and no accessory height is given

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: The 5 ft side and rear yards are given for all buildings in residential districts

spaces_required.note: 'All residential uses: one for each dwelling unit.' The unit is read as a dwelling unit

total_on_site.note: One for the house and one for the unit

min_lot_sqft.note: For a new lot by boundary adjustment or subdivision. An existing lot of at least 4,000 sq ft may be used for residential development (470-15A, 470-20B). New lots are 40 ft wide

setback_front_ft.note: 'Average of setbacks of adjoining lots on the block', set by the Zoning Officer

setback_side_ft.note: 'Minimum of 5 feet'. 'No building shall be less than 10 feet from an adjoining building.'

max_building_coverage.note: Building cover by lot size: 50% on 4,000 to 5,999 sq ft, 45% on 6,000 to 9,999 sq ft, 35% over 10,000 sq ft.
